rows.sprk_tooldescription: Summarize the session's documents AND save the summary onto the current matter record as a durable work product. Use when the user asks to save, persist, or file a summary to the matter (e.g. 'summarize this and save it to the matter', 'put the summary on the matter record'). Requires a matter-hosted session (the assistant embedded on a matter form); the summary is stored to the session ledger first, then persisted to the matter's Matter Summary (AI Work Product) field. For a chat-only summary that is NOT saved to the record, use the plain summarize capability instead. Optional arg: fileIds (subset of session file ids; omit to use all).

Explain this clause in plain language, using matter/firm playbook and precedent context where available. Read-only — returns an explanation, key concepts, and related playbook ids; does not edit the document.
Summarize the tracked changes a reviewer made in Word — insertions, deletions, comments, and structural edits — in plain language. Read-only.

Explain Spaarke's default NDA standard in plain language for a non-lawyer audience — what the firm typically requires in an NDA and why. Use when the user asks what the firm's standard NDA terms are, wants a plain-language explanation of Spaarke's NDA positions, or asks something like 'what does our NDA standard say about confidentiality' WITHOUT referencing a specific uploaded agreement. Does not review, redline, or reference any uploaded document — for reviewing an actual NDA against the standard, use the NDA Review capability instead. Not legal advice.
Compare this clause against the matter/firm playbook — surfaces matching entries, deviations from firm-standard language, and a risk score. Read-only.
Scan the document for defined terms and check they are used consistently. Read-only; results render in the Context pane.

Create a follow-up task (a Spaarke To Do / action item) from this conversation. Use when the user asks to create a task, to-do, follow-up, action item, or reminder about the session's documents, analyses, or findings (e.g. 'create a follow-up task to send this by Friday'). Requires a due date and an assignee — supply them from the conversation; if either is missing they will be elicited. RELATIVE DATE RULE: resolve relative due dates ('tomorrow', 'next Friday', 'in two weeks') against the current date given in the '## Current Date' context block — never guess the year — and state the resolved absolute date in the proposal. This capability DRAFTS the proposed task (title, description, priority suggestion, source citations) grounded in the session material — it does NOT create the record. After presenting the proposal to the user, create the record by calling dataverse.create_record with tablename 'sprk_event' and an item carrying: sprk_eventname (the proposal title), sprk_description (the proposal description PLUS a final provenance line that MUST name the source document file and the source analysis ledger key, e.g. 'Provenance: source document nda-acme.pdf; source analysis 651194cd-3670-f111-ab0e-70a8a590c51c@t3' — copy ledger keys VERBATIM from the '## Session Outputs (stored ledger)' context block), sprk_duedate (the resolved due date as yyyy-MM-dd), and sprk_eventtype_ref as a lookup {"relatedTable":"sprk_eventtype_ref","name":"Task","recordId":"124f5fc9-98ff-f011-8406-7c1e525abd8b"}. ASSIGNEE RULE: the assignee column is sprk_assignedto1 (a lookup to the contact table — recordId GUID REQUIRED). When the user names SOMEONE ELSE, resolve that person's contact GUID via dataverse.search_data or dataverse.read_query FIRST and set sprk_assignedto1; NEVER pass a lookup object without recordId — it will be rejected. When the task is for the requesting user themselves ('assign to me'): the record already belongs to them automatically; try to resolve THEIR contact record by their name/email if it appears in the conversation and set sprk_assignedto1 with the resolved GUID — if you cannot resolve it, OMIT the column and state the assignee's name inside sprk_description instead. REGARDING RULE: when this chat is hosted on a record (see the 'Context: This chat is hosted on…' line), also set the matching regarding lookup with the HOST record's id — sprk_regardingmatter for a matter, sprk_regardingproject for a project, sprk_regardinginvoice for an invoice, sprk_regardingaccount for an account, sprk_regardingcontact for a contact (e.g. {"relatedTable":"sprk_matter","recordId":"<host record id>"}). That write is confirmation-gated: it suspends for the user's explicit approval before executing, and after approval the created record's id and link are reported back in chat. POST-CONFIRMATION RULE: ask for confirmation in chat AT MOST ONCE — presenting the drafted proposal and asking once is the ONLY chat question allowed. The moment the user affirms the proposal ('yes', 'create it', 'confirm'), IMMEDIATELY invoke dataverse.create_record with the sprk_event contract above IN THAT SAME TURN — do NOT announce that you are about to proceed and ask again, do NOT re-invoke this capability to regenerate the draft. The CONFIRMATION DIALOG presented by dataverse.create_record is the approval step: invoke the write tool and let it suspend.

REFUSAL — call this when the user's request matches no other available capability or tool and cannot be answered from the session's documents or connected records with citations. Renders the platform's honest statement of what it can and cannot do; relay its returned message verbatim. Required arg: unsupported_request — a short neutral label (10 words or fewer) of what the user asked for (e.g. 'document translation'); do not copy the user's message verbatim. Terminal informational output — no side effects, never suspends.

rows.sprk_name: Invoice Line Code (UTBMS coding and observations)

rows.sprk_tooldescription: Use when the user asks what they need to do, wants to review or prioritize THEIR OWN tasks, or asks about their day, agenda, workload, open work, or deadlines — e.g. 'what do I need to do today', "what's on my plate", 'help me prioritize my tasks', 'what should I work on first', 'what are my tasks', 'show my open tasks', 'do I have any overdue items'. This capability reads the caller's own open, assigned tasks (plus their daily-briefing context) over their identity and PRODUCES A GROUNDED, CITED SUMMARY — real counts and the most pressing items — plus a short PRIORITIZED RECOMMENDATION, AND opens their task list in a workspace tab. It is the ONLY grounded source of the user's task data: whenever the user asks about their tasks, day, or what to do, prefer this over answering from memory, and NEVER state a task count or name without invoking it. Read-only — it never creates or modifies anything (to CREATE a task use create-task; for a to-do use create-todo; it never lists ANOTHER person's tasks).

Classify an uploaded document into a document-type label (nda, contract, invoice, ...) with a calibrated confidence score. Runs automatically as the first member of the document_uploaded event rule; its confidence gates the M4 confirmation policy before auto-summarization.

Summarize the file(s) the user uploaded into this chat session. Produces a structured summary (TL;DR bullets, narrative summary, keywords, named entities) rendered in the Assistant Workspace pane. Use when the user asks to summarize, recap, or get a TL;DR of uploaded/attached documents. Optional args: fileIds (subset of session files; defaults to all, max 20), styleHint (e.g. executive, detailed, bullet-points). Informational output only — no side effects.

Rewrite this clause to be more concise — remove redundancy and verbosity while preserving its exact legal meaning and obligations. Produces a pending track-change (a structured edit — the condensed replacement text plus a rationale) the attorney can accept, replace, or undo; it does not persist the edit until accepted.

rows.sprk_name: Invoice Code Set Match (code-set mapping proposals)

rows.sprk_tooldescription: Review an uploaded NDA (non-disclosure agreement) against the Spaarke firm NDA standard, clause by clause, and surface an advisory risk assessment. Use when the user asks to review, check, assess, or flag risks in an NDA they uploaded or attached (e.g. 'review this NDA', 'check this NDA against our standard', 'what's risky in this NDA'). Advisory output for attorney review — not legal advice. Produces an overall risk rating plus a per-clause finding list, each citing the exact NDA text and the firm-standard clause it is measured against; does not edit or redline the document (that is the separate Draft Alternative capability).

rows.sprk_name: Invoice Firm Notice (firm notice prose drafting)

rows.sprk_tooldescription: Create a new matter (a Spaarke sprk_matter record) from this conversation. Use when the user asks to create, open, start, or intake a matter, or says something like 'create a matter from this file, practice area <label>, type <label>'. This capability DRAFTS the proposed matter (name, description, practice-area/matter-type LABEL suggestions, source citations) grounded in the session material — it does NOT create the record. After presenting the proposal to the user, create the record by calling dataverse.create_record with tablename 'sprk_matter' and an item carrying: sprk_mattername (the proposal's matter name, or the user's stated name if they gave one), sprk_matterdescription (the proposal description PLUS a final provenance line that MUST name the source document file, e.g. 'Provenance: source document nda-acme.pdf' — copy file names VERBATIM from the session context). PRACTICE AREA / MATTER TYPE RULE: sprk_practicearea and sprk_mattertype are LOOKUPS to sprk_practicearea_ref / sprk_mattertype_ref (never multi-select choices, never free text) — before asking the user to confirm, resolve the practice-area/matter-type LABEL (from the proposal's suggestions or the user's own words) to its reference-row GUID via dataverse.read_query IN THE SAME TURN, and set {"relatedTable":"sprk_practicearea_ref","recordId":"guid"} (same pattern for sprk_mattertype_ref); if you cannot resolve a confident match, OMIT that column and mention the intended value inside sprk_matterdescription instead — never guess a GUID and never use '@odata.bind'. Records you create belong to the calling user automatically. POST-CONFIRMATION RULE: ask for confirmation in chat AT MOST ONCE — presenting the drafted proposal and asking once is the ONLY chat question allowed. The moment the user affirms the proposal ('yes', 'create it', 'confirm'), IMMEDIATELY invoke dataverse.create_record with the sprk_matter contract above IN THAT SAME TURN — do NOT announce that you are about to proceed and ask again, do NOT re-invoke this capability to regenerate the draft. The CONFIRMATION DIALOG presented by dataverse.create_record is the approval step: invoke the write tool and let it suspend.

Rewrite this clause according to a free-text instruction the user provides (e.g. 'make this mutual', 'add a 30-day cure period', 'change governing law to Delaware'). Produces a pending track-change (a structured edit — the rewritten clause text plus a rationale) the attorney can accept, replace, or undo; it does not persist the edit until accepted. Requires the free-text `instruction` argument, collected from the user at click time.

Re-run the analysis/summary on the document currently loaded in the workspace, reusing the document's existing analysis (the summarize Action). Use as the 'Reanalyze' follow-on chip on a loaded-document context to refresh the analysis on demand. Informational output only — no side effects.

Create a new project (a Spaarke sprk_project record) from this conversation. Use when the user asks to create, open, start, or set up a PROJECT (e.g. 'create a project from this file', 'start a new project for the Acme migration'). This capability DRAFTS the proposed project (name, description, practice-area and project-type LABEL suggestions, source citations) grounded in the session material — it does NOT create the record and does NOT ask follow-up questions in chat. After drafting, the proposal is handed to the Create Project wizard, opened PRE-SEEDED: the drafted name and description fill the wizard fields, and the practice-area / project-type are pre-selected from the deterministic constrained-field resolver's matches. The LLM NEVER resolves those closed-set lookups to GUIDs — it only suggests the LABEL; the resolver turns labels into the wizard's pre-selected dropdown values. The Create Project wizard owns the gated write, the source-file attach, assignment, and review — producing the real record. Do NOT call dataverse.create_record; do NOT resolve practice-area / project-type GUIDs via read_query; do NOT elicit fields in chat. Present the drafted project proposal and let the pre-seeded wizard take over. DISAMBIGUATION: a 'matter' is a DISTINCT capability (create-matter). Use this ONLY when the user specifically asks for a PROJECT; if they ask for a matter, use create-matter instead.

Revise the WHOLE document currently open in Compose. Use when the user asks to revise, review, align, or flag risks across the ENTIRE document they have open (e.g. 'align this whole contract with our playbook', 'flag any risky clauses in this document', 'clean up the clarity of this agreement', 'revise this document to tighten the indemnification language'). This is DIFFERENT from compose-draft-alternative (which rewrites only the ONE clause the user has selected/highlighted) and compose-draft-document (which drafts a BRAND-NEW document from scratch) — use this capability when the user wants an existing OPEN document reviewed or revised end-to-end. Produces pending track-change edits and/or anchored review comments the attorney accepts, replaces, resolves, or undoes; it does NOT persist any change until accepted. Required arg: revisionIntent (one of align-clauses, flag-risks, improve-clarity, custom — infer from the user's phrasing; default to improve-clarity if unclear). Optional arg: instruction (free-text refinement, required for custom).

Propose an alternative rewrite of this clause, grounded in matter/firm playbook and precedent context where available. Produces a pending track-change (a structured edit — replacement text plus rationale and sources) the attorney can accept, replace, or undo; it does not persist the edit until accepted.

Create a personal To Do (a Spaarke sprk_todo action item) from this conversation. Use this capability ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a 'to do', 'to-do', 'todo', or a personal checklist / reminder item — the lightweight personal-action sense — about the session's documents, analyses, or findings (e.g. 'add a to-do to send this by Friday', 'make a to-do for me to review the indemnity clause'). Do NOT use this to VIEW or LIST the user's existing tasks or to-dos (e.g. 'what are my tasks', 'show my open items') — that is the list-tasks capability. DISAMBIGUATION (Event-Task vs To Do, the authored ambiguity): if the user instead says 'task', 'event', 'meeting', 'appointment', or uses time-blocked / calendar language ('block time', 'schedule', 'at 3pm', 'on my calendar'), that is an Event-Task — use the create-task capability instead of this one. When the intent is genuinely ambiguous, prefer the user's explicit noun; if they said 'to do', choose this. Never negotiate the choice over multiple chat turns — draft the best single interpretation; the user can one-tap the 'Make it an Event-Task instead' chip to switch. This capability DRAFTS the proposed To Do (title, description, priority suggestion, source citations) grounded in the session material — it does NOT create the record and does NOT ask follow-up questions in chat. After drafting, the proposal is handed to the user's To Do create form, opened PRE-SEEDED, where the user sets the due date, assignee, and any parent record (regarding), reviews, and saves. Do NOT call dataverse.create_record; do NOT elicit a due date or assignee in chat — the form collects those. Present the drafted To Do and let the pre-seeded form take over.

DEFAULT capability for drafting. Use whenever the user asks to draft, write, compose, or prepare a letter, memo, report, response, notice, agreement, or any document — INCLUDING when they say to 'send a letter' to someone (a letter is a document, even if later sent). Examples: 'draft a client reporting letter', 'send a letter to opposing counsel', 'write a memo responding to this notice'. Opens a complete draft in the Compose editor to review, edit, redline, and save. Use this for ALL drafting UNLESS the user explicitly says 'email'.

Classifies an uploaded document into an agreement sub-domain (NDA, employment, lease, asset-purchase, ...) with per-candidate confidence, flags composite/multi-type documents, and flags non-agreement documents. Dispatched automatically by the Assistant when a user asks to review an uploaded document of unknown type; its structured result drives the Agreement Review confirmation gate (near-certain confidence auto-proceeds; below-threshold or composite confirms with the user first). Not intended for direct invocation and produces no user-facing narrative on its own.

rows.sprk_name: Billing Rule Draft (rule drafting from guidelines)

rows.sprk_tooldescription: Use ONLY when the user explicitly says EMAIL — e.g. 'draft an email', 'email the client', 'send an email to opposing counsel'. Produces email correspondence (subject, body, recipients). Do NOT use for letters, memos, or any document — even one the user intends to send; those go to compose-draft-document. The ONLY trigger for this capability is an explicit 'email' request.
